name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2025, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 7,400 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2025_contributionandallocationrates.pdf .

name: Chinese Development Assistance Council Fund
authority: CPF Board self-help group contribution schedule: Chinese Development Assistance Council Fund. Monthly employee-borne wage-band deductions apply to Chinese Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. The base includes cash wage allowances, overtime and leave encashment, less unpaid absence; official expense reimbursements are excluded. The published wage band applies unless a dated fund instruction records an opt-out or a different monthly amount. Explicit zero is distinct from no instruction. The instruction reference is required; MBMF changes use the approved total after any component changes. CPF Board: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups . CDAC employer FAQ 18 allows an employee with multiple jobs to opt out for selected employers: https://www.cdac.org.sg/cdac-funding-info-information-for-employers .

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. The three bands below carry the minimum, the rate and the maximum; the levy is employer-borne. A month in which no remuneration is payable attracts no levy, which is why the first band opens at SGD 0.01. Base: allowances are wages (CPF Act 1953 s.2 'wages': all remuneration in money including allowances; the SDL Order and the self-help-group schedules read total wages), so `ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward) is in every base; a reimbursement row must be excluded by name.

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. The three bands below carry the minimum, the rate and the maximum; the levy is employer-borne. A month in which no remuneration is payable attracts no levy, which is why the first band opens at SGD 0.01. Base: allowances are wages (CPF Act 1953 s.2 'wages': all remuneration in money including allowances; the SDL Order and the self-help-group schedules read total wages), so `ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward) is in every base; a reimbursement row must be excluded by name.

name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2025, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 7,400 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2025_contributionandallocationrates.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year .

rules.refusal: Record the employee’s residency status: CPF contributions are payable for every Singapore citizen and permanent resident employee (Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.7), so an unrecorded status cannot be read as outside CPF.

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. name: Central Provident Fund

First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2025, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 7,400 per month. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2027, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. name: Chinese Development Assistance Council Fund

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. The three bands below carry the minimum, the rate and the maximum; the levy is employer-borne. A month in which no remuneration is payable attracts no levy, which is why the first band opens at SGD 0.01. Base: allowances are wages (CPF Act 1953 s.2 'wages': all remuneration in money including allowances; the SDL Order and the self-help-group schedules read total wages), so `ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward) is in every base; a reimbursement row must be excluded by name.
assessed_on: BASE + OVERTIME + (ALLOWANCES + ADHOC) + ENCASHMENT - ABSENCE - NO_PAY_LEAVE

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.3 with the Skills Development Levy Order — 0.25% of the first SGD 4,500 of monthly remuneration, a minimum of SGD 2 for an employee earning less than SGD 800 a month and a maximum of SGD 11.25 for one earning more than SGD 4,500. The three bands below carry the minimum, the rate and the maximum; the levy is employer-borne. A month in which no remuneration is payable attracts no levy, which is why the first band opens at SGD 0.01. Base: allowances are wages (CPF Act 1953 s.2 'wages': all remuneration in money including allowances; the SDL Order and the self-help-group schedules read total wages), so `ALLOWANCES` and `ADHOC` (each class listing the scheme in its counts_toward) is in every base; a reimbursement row must be excluded by name.

name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year .

name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year .

rules.refusal: Record the employee’s residency status: CPF contributions are payable for every Singapore citizen and permanent resident employee (Central Provident Fund Act 1953 s.7), so an unrecorded status cannot be read as outside CPF.

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2027, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year .

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year .

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. Other student paths are not inferred from an internship label. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. The employer owes 0.25% of monthly money wages, minimum SGD 2 and maximum SGD 11.25. The local tertiary student exemption is priced from declared standing and institution approval; the overseas-tertiary and school-holiday classes remain separately under review. The CPF Board confirms the aggregate employer-month total is rounded down to the nearest dollar. Sources: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/SDLA1979#pr2- ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy .

name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2027, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning.
